questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: What motivated me to go on exchange to Melbourne was that I knew I wanted to go to Australia due to the culture, nature and people and furthermore I heard from friends and these travel reports, that Melbourne was the best city to live in. And I really think it lived up to that.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Living in a foreign city and being a student is something I will never forget, but the actual application process for going to Australia was really messy, and there was not much help to get.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was really easy upon arrival, because Monash University did a really good job with a lot of information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: At first we got a free transfer from the airport to our recommendation that the university paid for. Besides that we had an introduction day shortly after we arrived.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was actually really difficult, because acommendation is very expensive in Melbourne and therefore it took a long time to find something affordable. We lived in a Airbnb, was was affordable and also Facebook pages in Melbourne is a hack.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: We lived in the CBD close to the train station, so we could therefore easily go to Monash. I would highly recommend staying in the city, since Monash University is in the suburbs, and we only had to attend uni two times a week.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: This was actually also a bit confusing, but mostly because there were so many courses and you could select your scheme on your own, which was really nice.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of help available, such as two different helpcenters with different focuses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Really succesful! Since the university is so big, there were many different dates and times for each course to select from and the system differ from the danish, therefore you enroll yourself in the courses that fits you.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I attended the late arrival introduction, because I book my flight to early to know the exact arrival time, and therefore I would highly recommend to attend that and also to check your host institution email prior to arrival or prior to attending classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a bit sad that the lectures were online, which made it a bit different since I only had to be at uni two times a week and then watch the lectures from home.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were quite easy, but since all my units were elective courses, I had courses that were very different from my study programme at KU, which made some of the courses slightly difficult to follow, but nothing major.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. It was based on online lectures and a lot of homework regarding readings and sometimes quizzes, and then the tutorials required presentations and many discussions in the class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Understanding social behaviour 
Crime prevention and crime control 
Crime and inequality 
Interrogating racism: Indigenous Australians and the State

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all courses, but my favorite courses was Crime and inequality, because it shed light on topics and discussions in a very different way.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Mostly traveling costs from traveling around Australia, which is really expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was not as expensive as I thought, it was cheaper than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We joined a club, which was really nice!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were so many opportunities for all kind of clubs. We joined a surf club, but they have everything!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend joining a club for meeting other students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Do small trips around Melbourne, it is packed with the most amazing nature and options for both hiking, surfing etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was really easy, the locals were so sweet and really openminded. Since they have English as their first language, it is easy to meet people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs and attend the early arrival.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There was not many cultural differences that I can think of.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: What I enjoyed most about the culture was their openness towards other people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- To stay in the city if possible 
- Attend the clubs at uni if you want to meet new people 
- Use the city - because it is amazing!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's important to know that you can change your courses up to two weeks after you’ve started, which is really nice because it gives you a lot of flexibility — something I didn’t know before I went.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To meet many new people, learning about the Australian history and getting to feel safe and home in another city, which is an amazing experience and further all the options for doing trips throughout the week and weekends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was all the ongoing tests, assignments and quizzes, which I am not used to having at KU and also getting used to speaking English when taking part in discussions at uni.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
